classification_reasons: Spec is not tight enough to call routine even though both flagged concerns are now closed: the design settles a brand-new public function's error-handling contract (ValueError vs ZeroDivisionError vs 0.0) and its parameter-type contract (Collection[float], overturning the panel's own Sequence[float] pick) — exactly the kind of judgment call sdlc.yaml's routine bar excludes regardless of how settled the spec now reads.

Blast radius is small in file count (this diff, cumulative since merge-base, touches only changes/0002-add-mean-helper-to-sample-pkg/{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/**} — no sample_pkg/*.py, tests/*.py or guardrail file, no sdlc.yaml risk_list item), but that is because phase b writes no code; the function and its tests do not exist on disk yet.

No existing test covers `mean` (it does not exist yet); the 'code the existing tests already cover' leg of routine fails by construction at design time, so classification stays non-routine, unchanged from every prior round on this change.
attempted: Intent: re-read intent.md's Proposed outcome, Constraints and both Open questions against spec.md/plan.md as they stand at this head. Both open questions (empty-sequence behaviour, parameter type) are closed, and the closures match what intent asked for: a docstring-stated, test-covered empty-input behaviour and a minimal, unweighted, no-wrapper mean consistent with divide/percent. This round's own delta (status.yaml, run-b.json, evidence bookkeeping for registering a new fix cycle after the owner's third sdlc:reset-iterations label) touches none of intent's substance.

Spec and plan: read spec.md and plan.md in full. plan.md's Files/Order of work/Proof sections are internally consistent, name the exact files in the order plan.md lists them, and correctly carry both panel/owner decisions (ValueError guard clause; Collection[float] signature) into the concrete code shown in step 1. Found one real but non-blocking defect: spec.md's Flagged concerns bullets prepend 'decided (by panel): ...' / 'decided (owner, overturning the panel): ...' onto the original *undecided* framing without rewriting it, so each bullet still contains stale text ('Needs the panel's (or owner's) decision...', 'is undecided') alongside its own closure — self-contradictory prose. Separately, spec.md's Design section still says of the empty-input case 'This is not settled here either (Flagged concerns)', contradicting the Flagged concerns section's own closure of that same item. Neither defect changes what gets built: plan.md (what phase c actually implements from) states both decisions once, clearly, with no contradiction, and REVIEW.md reserves 'Important' for findings that would break behaviour, leak data or breach a policy, not for prose that fails to keep two sections of the same document in sync. Judged a nit, not a reason to escalate.

This round's own delta: per status.yaml (iterations: 1, iterations_reset_by: luissiviero) and evidence/run-b.json (started_at 2026-09-24T17:27:46Z), the change since the prior reviewed head is bookkeeping only — registering a new fix-round cycle after the owner reapplied sdlc:reset-iterations on PR #13. No spec.md/plan.md/decisions-b.* content differs from the state already reviewed and continued in the prior round.

Proof: at phase b no code exists yet, so there is no test.log/build.log/lint.log for `mean` to compare against a diff that adds tests — correct for a design phase. gate-b.json's committed 'commands' check shows build/test/lint green against the current, unmodified codebase (5 passed, no mean yet), which is literal toolchain output, not a claim, and is consistent with a design-only diff that adds no code.

Blast radius: confirmed via the diff's own diff --git headers and by directly reading status.yaml/spec.md/plan.md that every changed path stays under changes/0002-add-mean-helper-to-sample-pkg/; no .claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md or sdlc.yaml is touched; no sdlc.yaml risk_list item (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) applies to a pure in-process function with no endpoint, no external input, no secret and no network call.

Policies: re-read decisions-b.md/decisions-b.json for both panel items and spec.md's per-skill rows (coding-standards, security-baseline, ux-conventions, data-conventions, definition-of-done). The owner's overturn of concern 2 (Collection[float] over Sequence[float]) is faithfully reflected in spec.md's Requirements/Design/Flagged-concerns and in plan.md's signature, step 1 code and Options-not-taken section; no loaded policy skill is silently skipped or contradicted.

Tests: no test code exists at phase b, correctly (tests land in phase c). plan.md's Proof section and spec.md's Acceptance section agree on the same four tests (normal, single-element, empty, non-Sequence Collection via a set) and the same expected pass count (9); tests/test_flag.py and the five pre-existing tests are named as untouched. Nothing in this round could let a bug hide behind a weakened or missing test, since no test-bearing file changed.

Deliberately not used as a reason: the deterministic owner_actions check that parked the prior gate cycle over how an automation-authored iteration reset credits a repeat owner-label actor is the gate's own mechanism, re-run fresh after this verdict; it is not something this review evaluates or restates, and this round's own reasoning (fix-response.md round 6) about that gap is not cited here either.
